arguments.summary: A high-severity data exfiltration attempt was detected using DNS tunneling (TXT records) from an internal finance workstation (WS-FIN-042) to the malicious domain c2.evil-example.com. Rapid containment actions included adding a firewall deny rule, quarantining the host, performing full endpoint scans, resetting compromised user credentials, and executing an Ansible remediation playbook to remove tunneling artifacts. The incident was fully resolved with no evidence of data loss.

timeline.description: SIEM detected unusual DNS TXT queries from host WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.42) to domain c2.evil-example.com.
Process creation event observed: suspicious rundll32 execution from Temp directory on WS-FIN-042.
IDS generated critical alert (ET TROJAN Cobalt Strike Beacon C2 Activity) for traffic to external IP 198.51.100.23.
Failed Kerberos TGT request from WS-FIN-042 indicating possible credential misuse.
SMB access event showing lateral movement attempt to file server 10.0.5.50.
SOC analyst generated high severity alert for DNS tunneling exfiltration and initiated containment.
Firewall rule added to block traffic to c2.evil-example.com on all ports (bidirectional deny).
Compromised host WS-FIN-042 quarantined and full endpoint scan started.
User credentials for CORP\jsmith reset and MFA re-enabled.
Ansible remediation playbook executed to remove DNS tunneling artifacts and restore system integrity.
Post‑remediation validation completed; no further malicious activity observed. Incident closed.
